narrative:
The model has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **43% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this isn’t a guarantee, it’s high enough that the school has decided you should take extra remedial courses to help you succeed. Think of it like a warning sign—just as you’d pay attention if your car’s dashboard showed a low fuel light, this prediction is a signal to take action before things get harder.

The biggest factors pushing this prediction are three key areas. First, **your study time** stands out as a concern. Most students who don’t need remedial help study **2 to 5 hours a week**, but you’re studying **less than 2 hours**. That’s a significant gap—like showing up to a marathon with only a quarter of the training. Without enough focused effort, even the most motivated students can struggle to keep up.

Second, **your father’s education level** plays a role. While many students whose fathers have higher education or completed secondary school tend to do better, your father’s education falls in the lower category compared to peers who don’t need extra support. This doesn’t mean your father’s background is the reason you’re at risk, but it suggests that without additional guidance, you might face extra challenges in areas where other students have more built-in support.

Finally, **your past academic record** actually works *in your favor*—you haven’t failed any classes before, which is great! This is the only major factor pulling the prediction toward success, showing that you *can* perform well when given the right structure.

The remedial courses aren’t a punishment; they’re a chance to fill in gaps before they become bigger problems. Focus on increasing your study time, seek out extra help if needed, and use this opportunity to build stronger habits. Many students in your position have turned things around—this is your moment to do the same.
